# Tcl execution evidence

## Question

> Ordinary literal and dynamically named source errors, missing-command errors and instruction-labelled public error stacks are distinct producers. Source trace similarity cannot establish identical Native instruction or ABI execution.

> What exact result/errorInfo/errorCode/errorstack fields do the original literal-error, dynamic-error and ordinary missing-command source controls report on each pinned provider?

## Assumptions

Assumptions were not separately recorded in the retained capture.

Recorded scope and limits:

> The exact authored ASCII LF source includes original catches/emit procedure and runs unchanged under fresh full provider initialisation via the native202 counted-source driver. The launcher adds no surrounding source envelope. Labelled guest hex fields and VERSION/ORIGINAL driver rows are parsed by tag, retaining original Jim stdout ordering.

## Script

```tcl-visible
# Original ASCII LF source. No binary-produced command names or private headers.
proc emit {label value} {
    binary scan $value H* encoded
    puts "$label\t$encoded"
}
proc source_boom {a} {
    set b 1
    error "bad $a"
}
proc dynamic_boom {a} {
    set command error
    $command "bad $a"
}
foreach name {source_boom dynamic_boom} {
    set code [catch {$name Q} message]
    emit "$name.code" $code
    emit "$name.result" $message
    if {[info exists ::errorInfo]} {emit "$name.errorInfo" $::errorInfo}
    if {[info exists ::errorCode]} {emit "$name.errorCode" $::errorCode}
    set stackCode [catch {info errorstack} stack]
    emit "$name.stackCode" $stackCode
    emit "$name.stack" $stack
}
set code [catch {definitely_missing_command} message]
emit missing.code $code
emit missing.result $message
if {[info exists ::errorCode]} {emit missing.errorCode $::errorCode}
```
